name: Grim Finance GrimBoostVault depositFor reentrancy
summary: GrimBoostVault.depositFor(token, amount, user) took the deposit token as a caller-supplied parameter and minted shares around an unguarded external transferFrom call, so the attacker passed its own contract as the token and re-entered depositFor from that callback, minting eight tranches of vault shares against a single SpiritSwap BTC/WFTM LP deposit before burning them all in withdrawAll to drain the vault.

loss.notes: The $30 million figure is the rounded aggregate loss across Grim Finance vaults affected by the same depositFor reentrancy campaign. Rekt reports approximately $30 million and Beefy's incident report estimates $32 million; this record uses the conservative rounded estimate.

lastCodeChange.description: Direct deployment of the GrimBoostVault runtime executed in the exploit.

sources.note: Reviewed the successful exploit receipt, replayed execution trace, direct creation receipt, archive runtime at deployment and immediately before the exploit, pre-exploit trace state, commit-pinned reproduction, Rekt analysis, and Beefy's incident report. The trace calls GrimBoostVault.depositFor recursively eight times through the attacker-controlled token callback, mints 316.434974081378761303 shares against one real BTC/WFTM LP transfer, and burns those shares in withdrawAll. GrimBoostVault is a direct 8,488-byte runtime with hash 0x753e4cd9dd083db2dc40f090d11ad54008e2db79a6a1212ca3d096ae39556c89 at deployment and immediately before the exploit; its disassembly contains no DELEGATECALL, SELFDESTRUCT, or CREATE2. The creation transaction is a successful top-level EOA deployment. Published incident analyses attribute approximately $30 million to $32 million of aggregate Grim vault losses to the same depositFor defect.

limitations: Published reports round the campaign-wide loss to approximately $30 million or $32 million; the record uses the conservative $30 million estimate.
